previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic venous insufficiency, lipodermatosclerosis, prosthetic heart valve, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for nausea, chills, and abdominal pain. She was found to have Group B streptococcal bacteremia, likely originating from her chronic leg skin changes. She was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and vancomycin initially, then transitioned to amoxicillin after pathogen identification. Her symptoms resolved, and she completed four days of IV antibiotics before discharge. She was prescribed a 10-day course of oral amoxicillin to complete treatment. An echocardiogram showed no valvular infection. Her INR was subtherapeutic, prompting a warfarin dose adjustment. She improved clinically and was discharged home with follow-up arranged.
problems: Streptococcus, group B, as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with h/o lipodermatosclerosis c/b recurrent cellulitis and 
bacteremia admitted for malaise, rigors, and hypotension 
concerning for sepsis. She was found to have possible RLE 
cellulitis but blood cultures, MRSA screen, and other infectious 
workup was negative. Her symptoms improved rapidly with 
vancomycin/ceftazidime, and she was narrowed to PO 
amoxicillin/clavulanate and discharged at baseline functional 
status.

=================
ACTIVE ISSUES
=================

# Malaise, rigors
Likely due to viral syndrome since blood cultures and other 
infectious workup was negative. She was treated initially with 
IVF and broad-spectrum antibiotics given concern for recurrent 
bacteremia and sepsis.

# Possible RLE cellulitis
No evidence for abscess on exam. MRSA screen negative. Treated 
initially with vancomycin/ceftazidime given history of MRSA and 
Pseudomonas, later narrowed due amoxicillin/clavulanate.

# Superficial anal laceration
Course was complicated by superficial perianal laceration from 
accidental trauma on commode. She was evaluated by Colorectal 
Surgery and underwent flexible sigmoidoscopy which found no 
further injuries. Warfarin and aspirin were held for 24 hours, 
and she was briefly bridged with heparin.

# Anticoagulation
On warfarin and aspirin at home for paroxysmal atrial 
fibrillation, h/o TIA, bioprosthetic AVR. INR was 
sub-therapeutic and she was briefly bridged with IV heparin 
(CHADS2Vasc=7, h/o TIA).

# Antibiotic-associated diarrhea
No leukocytosis or abdominal pain to suggest C diff. BP, renal 
function, and electrolytes remained stable. She was treated with 
loperamide and probiotics were recommended on discharge.

# Chronic diastolic heart failure (EF 60%)
# Bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement
Home torsemide and metoprolol were initially held due to concern 
for sepsis but later restarted. Weight and edema remained 
stable.

# Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
# h/o bradycardic arrest s/p pacemaker
No arrhythmias this admission. Anticoagulation and metoprolol 
per above.

# h/o DVT
Bilateral ___ dopplers negative in ED. No signs/symptoms of PE. 
Anticoagulation per above.

====================
CHRONIC ISSUES
====================

# Lipodermatoscleroris
Topical anti-inflammatory medications were initially held due to 
concern for worsening cellulitis, and were restarted on 
discharged.

# Chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency
No evidence for acute flare or contribution to presenting 
symptoms. No endocrine insufficiency (A1c 6.0% in ___. Home 
Creon was continued.

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___.

You were admitted because we were worried you had a skin 
infection (cellulitis) and possible blood infection 
(bacteremia).

- We gave you IV antibiotics and your symptoms improved
- We did blood cultures that showed you probably did not have 
another infection in the blood
- Unfortunately had an injury sitting on the commode. You were 
evaluated by our Colorectal specialists who did a sigmoidoscopy 
and luckily found you had no serious injury.
- We adjusted your blood thinners.

Instructions for when you go home:

- Take your antibiotics (""amoxicillin/clavulanate"") every 12 
hours until you finish the bottle on ___.

- Take a probiotic and loperamide as needed to help with the 
diarrhea caused by the antibiotics.

- When the diarrhea stops, you can take a stool softener and try 
___ baths twice daily to avoid irritating the cut on your 
bottom.

- We increased your warfarin dose a little bit. Take 3 mg every 
day unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Get your INR checked 
as directed by your doctor.

- Continue taking all of your other medications just like 
before.

- Weigh yourself every morning. Call your doctor if your weight 
goes up more than 3 pounds.

We wish you all the best!

Sincerely,
Your ___ Care Team
